reports.summary: A 42-year-old man received an £800 fine after police found about 127 grams of cannabis resin during a foot patrol.[@1] He appeared in the Magistrates’ Court the morning after his arrest and was charged with possession of a Class B drug.[@1] The case came under the current criminal code, which allows fines or imprisonment for possession.[@2]

reports.title: Samoa orders armed police on drug raids
reports.summary: The government ordered police to be armed during drug raids after drugs were found in boxes of frozen chicken, and the prime minister called drug trafficking a top priority. The order was an enforcement response, not a change in the Narcotics Act.

reports.title: Sana'a court sentences a hashish dealer to death
reports.summary: The Specialized Criminal Court in Sana'a sentenced Ahmed Abed al-Dhabian to death for buying, possessing, transporting and selling hashish, and ordered his movable and immovable property confiscated. A second defendant received 25 years for drug trafficking, and three others five years each for possessing hashish with intent to use.

reports.title: Abu Dhabi appeal court cuts a cannabis life sentence to three months
reports.summary: Abu Dhabi's Court of Appeal overturned a life sentence for possessing cannabis and psychotropic substances with intent to traffic and reclassified the offence as possession for personal use. The court found no evidence of promotion, negotiation or delivery, and said the investigation did not explain why police had concluded he was trading.

reports.title: Police seize 222 kg of hashish in Badakhshan
reports.summary: Police in Kishim district, Badakhshan, arrested two people and seized 222 kilograms of hashish from a vehicle disguised as a livestock carrier. The provincial police spokesman said the men were handed to judicial authorities. It was one of the largest single cannabis seizures reported in northern Afghanistan in 2025.

reports.title: Šamac police arrest a suspect after finding 3.8 kg of marijuana
reports.summary: Republika Srpska police arrested one person and reported finding 3.8 kg of suspected marijuana during a court-authorised search. The suspect was referred to the Doboj prosecutor the following day.

reports.title: Antsohihy gendarmes report 1,440 kg seized over six months
reports.summary: The Sofia gendarmerie reported 1,440 kg of cannabis in 114 sacks seized around Antsohihy over six months, with 10 arrests. The stock was burned on 8 December, and another 400 kg was seized the same afternoon.

reports.title: Police in northern Cyprus arrest ten people in two days of drug operations
reports.summary: In operations on 4 and 5 December 2025 in Kyrenia, Lefke, Metehan, Nicosia and at Ercan Airport, police reported seizing about 3.5 kg of drugs, most of it cannabis, including about 2 kg from a 22-year-old in Metehan and 600 g in Kyrenia, and arresting ten suspects. Two of them were held at the airport over four cannabis cigarettes after a detection dog alerted officers.

reports.title: Serbia indicts two defendants over the Zemun cannabis seizure
reports.summary: Belgrade’s Higher Public Prosecutor said it filed an indictment against two defendants in the case involving two tonnes of cannabis seized in Zemun. The indictment followed the investigation opened in August.

reports.title: Cannabis cultivation spreads in southern Sagaing
reports.summary: The Irrawaddy reported that villages in Ayadaw township and along the Myinmu border had shifted from rice, beans, betel nut and cotton to cannabis since 2022–23. Residents estimated at least five acres per village and more than thirty acres across six villages.

reports.title: Morocco's elite police seize 16 tonnes of hashish on the Atlantic coast
reports.summary: The Central Bureau of Judicial Investigations broke up a network that was using beaches near Casablanca to load hashish onto inflatable boats. Officers seized 16 tonnes of resin, six boats and eight engines in raids in Kenitra and Casablanca, and arrested eight people including two women. The operation was based on intelligence from the DGST.

reports.title: Chad's police burn seized cannabis under the 1995 drug law
reports.summary: The national police burned seized goods in the 7th district of N'Djamena, including 32 kg of cannabis herb, 34 balls of cannabis and 200 kg of psychotropic substances, beside 7.5 tonnes of adulterated alcohol. The deputy prosecutor present said the destruction complied with Law 22/PR/95 on drug control.

reports.title: Iraq says it dismantled 1,201 drug networks in three years
reports.summary: The interior ministry said security forces broke up 1,201 trafficking and dealing networks, including 171 international ones, and seized 14 tonnes of narcotics in the three years to November 2025. It counted 23,118 court judgments in drug cases, among them 300 death sentences and 1,147 life sentences, and said 6,022 people had recovered from addiction while 1,228 were in treatment at 16 centres.

reports.title: South Korea launches a joint drug investigation headquarters
reports.summary: The government set up a joint drug-crime investigation headquarters bringing prosecutors, police, customs and the intelligence service together, after smuggling and online sales rose. In its first 100 days it booked 124 people and detained 56, including a soldier who smuggled 10.2 kg of cannabis from Thailand and a farmer who grew cannabis under a state-funded smart farm.

reports.title: Bahrain upholds life for a 350 kg hashish network
reports.summary: The High Criminal Court in November 2025 rejected a challenge to a life sentence for a man convicted in a network that brought about 350 kg of hashish into Bahrain by sea between 2021 and 2023. Six other defendants, including a woman, were named in the case; the court treated the challenge to an in-absentia judgment as having no legal basis.

reports.title: Lebanon arrests a sanctioned cannabis and Captagon trafficker
reports.summary: The army arrested Nouh Zeaiter, a US-sanctioned Captagon and cannabis trafficker, at Kneiseh in Baalbek-Hermel. He had admitted cannabis cultivation and trafficking. The arrest was one of several against Bekaa networks in 2025.

reports.title: Gaza police seize hashish and cannabis plants in Zeitoun
reports.summary: Gaza's anti-narcotics police raided a home in Zeitoun, south of Gaza City, and seized 21 slabs of hashish, 317 Rotana pills, five marijuana plants, a rifle and ammunition. Two suspects were arrested; the police said drug flows into Gaza had risen since the war.

reports.title: A car from Iran brings 100 kg of hashish
reports.summary: Customs and drug-control officers stopped a Kuwaiti citizen returning from Iran on the Shuwaikh ferry and found more than 100 kilograms of hashish and marijuana in hidden compartments in his car. The case pointed to Iran as a source of resin shipped across the Gulf. The suspect was referred to the narcotics prosecution.

reports.title: Dominica's police burn seized cocaine and cannabis
reports.summary: Police destroyed drugs valued at about 53 million East Caribbean dollars in November 2025. Cannabis accounted for about 1.2 million of that and cocaine for about 52 million.

reports.title: Maldives launches its largest anti-drug operation
reports.summary: Operation Alimagu began on 13 November 2025 with about 500 officers raiding 110 places on 39 islands; police said 110 people were arrested on the first day. By late December they had searched 166 locations and nine vessels, arrested 193 people, and seized 30.63 kg of drugs and 182 bottles of alcohol.

reports.title: An underground greenhouse and 283 plants lead to a drug charge
reports.summary: The Interior Ministry arrested a previously convicted man after finding a greenhouse built underground on land beside his home. Police seized 283 cannabis plants and about 3 kilograms of dried marijuana, along with packaging materials, adhesive tape and an electronic scale.

reports.title: Police in Benin stop 130 kg of cannabis hidden as maize
reports.summary: Police in Bohicon arrested two motorcyclists coming from Azovè with 130 kg of cannabis in 237 slabs, packed in six sacks made to look like bags of maize. The men were handed to the central anti-drug office, Ocertid, for investigation.

reports.title: 97,000 cannabis plants destroyed in North Aceh
reports.summary: Indonesia's national narcotics agency led 151 officers into six fields near the village of Teupin Rusep and destroyed about 97,000 plants, some 69 tonnes by wet weight, on 6.5 hectares.

reports.title: BNN burns 69 tonnes of cannabis in North Aceh
reports.summary: Six plots covering 6.5 hectares in Teupin Reusep, North Aceh, held about 97,000 cannabis plants and 69 tonnes wet weight; 151 personnel destroyed them in place on 6 November 2025. The village is one of four alternative-development pilot sites where BNN is trying to move growers to legal crops.

reports.title: Kerala High Court says cannabis in pots is still cultivation
reports.summary: On 4 November 2025 the Kerala High Court refused to quash a prosecution against a man who grew five cannabis plants in pots on a rented terrace in Thiruvananthapuram. The court held that ‘cannabis plant’ means any plant of the genus, whether or not it bears flowering tops, and that growing it in a pot is cultivation under sections 8(b) and 20(a).

reports.title: British teenager freed in Georgia after a plea deal over 14 kg of cannabis
reports.summary: Bella May Culley, 19 and pregnant, faced life in prison for bringing 12 kg of marijuana and 2 kg of hashish into Tbilisi. Under a plea deal she was sentenced to the time she had already served and fined 500,000 lari.

reports.title: Morocco says its illegal cannabis fields have shrunk by 85 percent
reports.summary: The interior ministry's 2025 performance report put illegal cannabis cultivation at 20,627 hectares, down from about 134,000 hectares in 2003. It presented the fall as part of its supply-reduction strategy alongside the legal programme. The area remains far larger than the 3,141 hectares in legal production that year, and the figure is a government estimate rather than an independent survey.

reports.title: Nueva Alianza 53: 309 hectares of cannabis destroyed on Paraguay's border
reports.summary: Over ten days, Paraguay's anti-drug agency and Brazil's Federal Police destroyed 309 hectares of cannabis, 96 growers' camps and more than 39 tonnes of the drug in the forests of Canindeyú, Caaguazú and Alto Paraná. Senad says the phase kept at least 966 tonnes of cannabis out of the Brazilian market, where it estimates the crop would have earned USD 144 million.

reports.title: Montenegro police arrest a third suspect in the Trnovo cannabis case
reports.summary: Police arrested a 31-year-old man from Bar, identified as N.D., on suspicion of drug production and supply in the Trnovo investigation.[@1] The August operation had uncovered about 13,100 cannabis plants and led to two arrests.[@1] Investigators said they were continuing to identify people involved in cultivation and distribution; further complaints followed in March 2026.[@1,2]

reports.title: Hadramout court sentences six Iranians to death over three tonnes of hashish
reports.summary: The Specialized Criminal Court in Hadramout sentenced six Iranian nationals to death for smuggling nearly three tonnes of hashish and crystal methamphetamine from Iran into Yemeni waters. The court ordered the drugs destroyed and the seized items confiscated, and the justice ministry said the case was part of efforts against transnational organised crime.

reports.title: Bahrain's top court upholds a 10-year sentence for CBD vapes
reports.summary: The Court of Cassation in October 2025 upheld a 10-year prison sentence and BHD5,000 fine for a man convicted over electronic shishas containing cannabis after customs officers at the King Fahd Causeway found the devices and containers holding suspected CBD. Two co-defendants received one year and BHD1,000 each. The case began in 2024 and the suspected CBD liquid was prosecuted as cannabis.

reports.title: Police report 61 kg of cannabis arriving at Albania’s airport
reports.summary: State Police announced two arrests at Rinas and the seizure of 61 kg of suspected cannabis in four suitcases. They said the shipment had come from Bangkok and was intended for sale in Albania.

reports.title: Jordan seizes 119 blocks of hashish in border and city raids
reports.summary: Jordan's Public Security Directorate announced twelve arrests in a series of drug operations on 20 October 2025. At the Jaber border crossing with Syria, officers seized 85,000 narcotic pills, and searches across the country recovered 119 blocks of hashish, including 40 in Jerash and 36 in Aqaba. The operations also led to arrests in Amman and Zarqa, where officers found further hashish and pills.

reports.title: Ivorian customs stop 74 kg of cannabis at the entrance to Abidjan
reports.summary: A mobile customs unit stopped a ride-hailing car coming from Aboisso on the Moossou bridge and found 78 balls and 40 slabs of cannabis, 74 kg in all. The driver and two passengers were detained.

reports.title: Paro court jails airport cannabis smugglers for five to six years
reports.summary: In August 2025 the Paro District Court sentenced a 33-year-old Indian national to six years for bringing more than 7 kg of cannabis through Paro airport from Bangkok. In October it sentenced three Indian nationals to between five years and five years and six months for a separate haul of more than 7 kg on the same route.

reports.title: Cannabis association challenges herbicide spraying of dagga fields
reports.summary: The Eswatini Cannabis Association demanded an immediate halt to aerial and drone spraying of cannabis fields with herbicides, alleging paraquat, glyphosate and dicamba use without environmental assessment or registered applicators. Police continued Operation Thunder, destroying fields and seizing hundreds of kilograms.

reports.title: Macau seizes more than 30 kg of cannabis at the airport
reports.summary: Police found 56 vacuum-sealed packets of cannabis buds, more than 30 kg, in the luggage of two Malaysian men who had flown in from South Korea. A Hong Kong man travelling with them was also arrested.

reports.title: Lebanon's army kills a clan member in a Bekaa drug raid
reports.summary: A drone strike attributed to the Lebanese Army in Dar al-Wassaa near Yammouneh killed Hassan Abbas Jaafar, a member of the Jaafar clan wanted for drug trafficking, killings and attacks on soldiers; two other clan members were wounded. The army did not mention the strike, saying soldiers returned fire during raids and killed a wanted man.

reports.title: Police destroy more than 10 tonnes of cannabis in Auckland grow-house raids
reports.summary: Police announced on 25 September 2025 that a month-long operation in Auckland had shut 120 cannabis grow houses, destroyed more than 11,000 plants and seized more than 10 tonnes of cannabis. Thirty people were arrested, most Vietnamese nationals facing deportation, and police put the black-market value at more than NZ$50 million.

reports.title: Taiwan rounds up 245 people in a nationwide cannabis sweep
reports.summary: On 23 and 24 September 2025 prosecutors, police and military police searched 330 places in 20 jurisdictions and arrested 245 people for growing, using or possessing cannabis. They seized 1.68 kg of cannabis, 83 cannabis products, 97 vape pods and 581 pieces of paraphernalia. The High Prosecutors' Office said the operation was meant to uncover hidden users and reject calls for legalisation.

reports.title: Kabul court jails seventeen for cannabis, tablets and alcohol
reports.summary: Kabul's primary court for narcotics and intoxicants sentenced seventeen people to seven months to three and a half years in prison and 15 to 35 lashes for selling and trafficking narcotic tablets, alcohol and cannabis. The Supreme Court approved the sentences, which were carried out on 23 September 2025.

reports.title: Police break up a 1,337-plant cannabis farm in Kakheti
reports.summary: Prosecutors charged five people after police found 1,337 cannabis plants, weighing more than 143 kilograms, in the village of Vakiri in Sighnaghi municipality. Searches of homes linked to the suspects also turned up 3.3 kilograms of dried marijuana already packaged, drying equipment and digital scales.

reports.title: Dubai appeal court clears Filipina over cannabis extract
reports.summary: Dubai's Court of Appeal acquitted a 35-year-old Filipina who had been sentenced to 10 years and a AED 100,000 fine for bringing 20 grams of cannabis extract into the country. Customs found the extract in 20 vape cartridges hidden in pancake-mix packages at Terminal 3 on 15 December 2024.

reports.title: Egypt's police raid a desert drug farm in Ismailia
reports.summary: The Interior Ministry announced the seizure of 27.5 tonnes of narcotics at a desert farm in Ismailia: 21 tonnes of fully grown plants and 6.5 tonnes in hidden storage, valued at about 1.6 billion Egyptian pounds. One suspect was found with 90 kg of hashish and 10 kg of hydro, and firearms were seized.

reports.title: Oman's airports seize marijuana from a run of arriving passengers
reports.summary: Customs officers at Salalah airport found 11.65 kilograms of marijuana in the baggage of two Indian travellers on 23 July 2025, then 6.5 kilograms in another Indian traveller's luggage five days later. At Muscat airport, officers reported 12.66 kilograms from a Chinese woman on 21 August and, on 13 September, 9 kilograms from one traveller and 8 kilograms hidden in food bags from another.

reports.title: A prison inmate runs a 145 kg hashish ring
reports.summary: Police broke up a hashish network holding 145 kilograms of resin and arrested a female suspect, then searched the cell of a non-Kuwaiti inmate who ran the gang from Central Prison. Another accomplice was at large outside Kuwait. The case showed that prison-based dealers can direct smuggling networks beyond the walls.

reports.title: Kuwait reports 527 trafficking cases in eight months
reports.summary: The Interior Ministry said 527 drug-trafficking cases involving 823 suspects had been recorded since January, alongside 1,359 abuse cases against 1,675 people. Seizures included 959 kilograms of hashish and 142 kilograms of marijuana, far more resin than herbal cannabis, as well as 391 kilograms of methamphetamine and 6.8 million Lyrica capsules. The figures cover all drugs, not cannabis alone.

reports.title: Oman police find 85 kg of hashish and marijuana on the Quriyat coast
reports.summary: Police arrested two people linked to international trafficking networks after finding more than 85 kilograms of hashish and marijuana, plus 70,000 psychotropic tablets, at a coastal hideout in Quriyat. The Royal Oman Police said the drugs had been loaded into a vehicle for trafficking and consumption. The statement did not split the cannabis between resin and herb or name the source country.

reports.title: Lebanon's army destroys cannabis fields in the northern Bekaa
reports.summary: Army units destroyed cannabis fields in Zarazir, Deir al-Ahmar and Shleefa in the northern Bekaa, including plants grown inside homes, and arrested a suspect. The raids came the same week the government appointed the Cannabis Regulatory Authority. They were enforcement, not a change in the law.

reports.title: Serbia investigates two suspects after a two-tonne cannabis seizure
reports.summary: Belgrade’s Higher Public Prosecutor said it opened an investigation against two suspects after two tonnes of cannabis packaged for further sale were seized in Zemun. The office later linked its continuing investigation to the five-tonne seizure near Kruševac in January 2026.

reports.title: Guinea's gendarmes seize 1,725 kg of cannabis in a minibus
reports.summary: The gendarmerie's research brigade in Kindia intercepted a minibus on the road from Bambaya carrying 1,725 kg of cannabis; the driver abandoned it and was arrested four days later. The operation was part of an anti-drug campaign launched by the prosecutor general at the Conakry court of appeal, and the Kindia prosecutor was informed.

reports.title: Cambodia reports nearly 15,000 drug arrests in seven months
reports.summary: A report by Cambodia's Anti-Drug Department counted 14,977 people arrested for drug offences between January and July 2025, 2.7% more than in the same period a year earlier; 537 of them were foreigners. Seizures included 505 kg of dried cannabis and 12,212 fresh cannabis plants, out of 1.91 tonnes of drugs in all.

reports.title: Zhambyl police cut and burn 3,000 tonnes of wild cannabis
reports.summary: By mid-August 2025, during the Karasora operation, police in Zhambyl region mowed wild cannabis on 4,394.6 hectares of steppe and burned the cut plants. The regional police put the total weight at more than 3,000 tonnes. The work used agricultural machinery and was part of the annual campaign against harvesting in the Chu valley and nearby areas.

reports.title: Japan seizes a record tonne of cannabis hidden in a container
reports.summary: Narcotics agents said on 13 August 2025 that they had seized 1.046 tonnes of dried cannabis, worth about 5.2 billion yen on the street, from a shipping container that had left Vietnam in May and arrived in Japan in June.[@1] It was the largest single seizure of any illegal drug in Japan, and more than twice the 452 kg of herbal cannabis recorded across the country in 2024.[@1]

reports.title: Libyan counter-terrorism forces arrest two men with hashish in Misrata
reports.summary: Libya's Counter-Terrorism Forces arrested two Nigerian nationals in Misrata on suspicion of drug trafficking, finding hashish, hallucinogenic pills and cash, according to a statement by the monitoring group Migrant Rescue Watch. The case was referred to the public prosecution.

reports.title: Kokopo police find 40 kg of marijuana with police and army uniforms
reports.summary: Police in Kokopo, East New Britain, seized 40 kg of marijuana in three green bags that also held Papua New Guinea Defence Force and police uniforms. The bags were found in the bush at Bitapabeke and Ulagunan after a group of young people fled; no one was arrested at the time. Police said the suspects' identities were known and appealed for them to surrender.

reports.title: Bahrain keeps life terms for a six-year cannabis farm
reports.summary: The High Criminal Appeals Court on 2 August 2025 upheld life sentences for the first two defendants in a cannabis-growing operation run from a rented villa in Adliya, and cut the third defendant's life term to 15 years; a fourth received 10 years and a fifth one year.

reports.title: Venezuela seizes three tonnes of marijuana on a boat in Falcón
reports.summary: Diosdado Cabello, the vice-president for security, announced the seizure of 3,077 kg of marijuana at Pico de Zamuro in Falcón state. Eight Venezuelans travelling in a boat with five high-powered engines were arrested by the investigative police's anti-drug division.

reports.title: São Tomé police arrest three in a park with cannabis and amphetamines
reports.summary: Judicial police arrested three men in Parque Popular with about 30 grams of liamba, or cannabis, and three doses of amphetamines.[@1] Two were São Toméan and one Portuguese; all were suspected of trafficking, and the judicial authorities imposed bail.[@1] RSTP’s August report quoted a police announcement and recalled the previous year’s raids on cannabis fields and sales points.[@1]

reports.title: Tunisia plans saliva tests for drug-driving
reports.summary: Colonel Sami Saoudi of the National Road Safety Observatory announced on 27 July 2025 that police would get rapid saliva tests for drugs, to be used at road checks and after traffic offences. No start date was given. The device would sit alongside alcohol tests; no THC threshold or separate penalty for cannabis was published.

reports.title: Mongolian police raid nightclubs and test 1,043 people positive
reports.summary: Police raided nightclubs and bars in Ulaanbaatar from 25 to 27 July 2025 and tested 1,043 people positive for an illicit drug. The campaign followed a rise in drug crime and calls for tougher enforcement. It was an enforcement operation, not a change in the law.

reports.title: Police find 15 cannabis plants after stopping a man with a packet
reports.summary: Police in Ochamchira stopped a 31-year-old local man in July 2025 and found a packet of cannabis on him. He led officers to a plot in the forest near Elyr where he had grown 15 South Krasnodar cannabis plants. A criminal case was opened and he was placed under house arrest. The case shows that a small outdoor plot is prosecuted as a crime, not treated as a minor infraction.

reports.title: Libyan forces seize five tonnes of hashish and break up a growing network
reports.summary: Security forces raided a network in the Green Mountain near Taknes, about 127 km east of Benghazi, at dawn on 19 July. They seized five tonnes of hashish and broke up what officials called a cannabis cultivation and processing operation, arresting several people.

reports.title: A nightclub assault puts drug enforcement in the spotlight
reports.summary: A fight outside an Ulaanbaatar nightclub on 18 July 2025 left a man badly injured; three suspects were arrested and a fourth, the chief executive of Gobi Cashmere, left the country. The assailants were reported to have been under the influence of illegal drugs, though no drug was named.

reports.title: Kikori police seize 125.6 kg of marijuana bound for Australia
reports.summary: Gulf police arrested nine people after finding seven bags holding 125.6 kg of marijuana at Kikori on 13 July 2025. Police said the load came from the Southern Highlands and was to be taken by dinghy and road towards Daru and then Australia through Saibai, Cairns and Townsville.

reports.title: Oman's prosecutors count 6,741 drug cases over two years
reports.summary: The Public Prosecution said 6,741 drug cases were recorded in Oman between 2023 and 2024, with 2024 higher than 2023. Its spokesman named hashish, shabu, heroin and painkillers as the most common drugs and said international networks used social media to recruit young people. The figures cover all drugs, not cannabis alone, and no arrest or conviction breakdown was published.

reports.title: Liechtenstein court retains a fine after testing imported THC vapes
reports.summary: After an earlier judgment was partly overturned, testing found 63–65% THC in three sampled vapes from a seized consignment. A combined CHF2,400 fine remained, with CHF600 expert costs; the reported judgment was still open to appeal.

reports.title: Gibraltar records 169 drug-possession offences in its policing year
reports.summary: The police authority’s 2024/25 table records 169 possession offences and 22 supply offences across all drugs. Its report describes enforcement ranging from possession fines to prison for trafficking.

reports.title: A Kuwaiti home grow earns a life sentence
reports.summary: The Criminal Court sentenced a Kuwaiti man to life in prison for growing marijuana in his Salwa apartment and selling it. Police found 45 plants and four kilograms of prepared cannabis, along with 37 kilograms of gold bars and precious metals that investigators treated as proceeds. The sentence was passed under the 1983 drug law, five months before its replacement took effect.

reports.title: Nicosia court hears of 42 people benefiting from supervised release
reports.summary: At Nicosia’s judicial-year closing session, supervised-release board member Mustafa Hidayet reported 42 beneficiaries between 18 September 2023 and 30 June 2025, with programmes for 36 people continuing. The figures concerned drug cases generally and were presented at the Nicosia court session.[@1]

reports.title: Zambia reports 4,728 drug arrests and 43.2 tonnes of cannabis
reports.summary: The Drug Enforcement Commission reported 4,728 arrests and 43.2 tonnes of cannabis seized in 2024, alongside 27.9 kg of codeine and 1.9 kg of cocaine. The figures cover all drugs and all forms of cannabis, not cannabis alone.

reports.title: The Gambia's drug agency reports four tonnes of cannabis seized
reports.summary: The director general of the Drug Law Enforcement Agency reported 1,219 people arrested in 1,208 drug cases in 2024, 1,014 of them Gambians. The agency seized 1.9 tonnes of cannabis sativa and 2.2 tonnes from plantations; cannabis made up 54.7% of all seizures.

reports.title: Myanmar's junta burns a year's seized drugs
reports.summary: At ceremonies in Yangon, Mandalay and Taunggyi, the home affairs ministry destroyed drugs valued at about 1,072 billion kyats. Among them were over 597 kg of marijuana, beside 1,744 kg of heroin, over 1,334 kg of opium, over 8,573 kg of ketamine and 281 million methamphetamine tablets. The drugs had been seized between 1 June 2024 and 31 May 2025.

reports.title: Brunei arrests five cannabis couriers who flew to Europe
reports.summary: Five Bruneian men aged 22 to 38 were arrested for carrying 68 kg of cannabis to Europe through third countries, earning about B$21,000. They used modified luggage, and the case showed Brunei acting as a courier source rather than only a consumer market. The arrests were an enforcement action, not a change in the law.

reports.title: Police trace marijuana smuggled through Port Moresby airport
reports.summary: Police reported arresting a couple and a taxi driver from Hela with 13 kg of marijuana that had arrived from the Highlands, and finding about 10 kg left unattended after a flight from Tapini. They were also investigating more than eight bags that arrived on an Air Sanga flight in May and disappeared from the terminal with the help of airport and police officers.

reports.title: Honduras's army reports 180,000 marijuana plants seized in half a year
reports.summary: The Honduran armed forces said they had secured 13 illegal marijuana fields with about 180,000 plants so far in 2025, beside 37 coca plantations with more than 770,000 bushes. The latest marijuana field, at Tocoa in Colón, held about 36,000 plants on eight manzanas.

reports.title: Malta's cannabis authority starts handling odour complaints
reports.summary: After the May amendments took effect, the Authority for the Responsible Use of Cannabis opened a freephone line for complaints about cannabis smells from private homes. Complaints must be signed and say where the smell comes from; officers first advise, then enforce the €235 fine if the nuisance continues.

reports.title: 70 kg of cannabis found in transit luggage at Beijing airport
reports.summary: In June 2025 customs officers at Beijing Capital International Airport found 70.83 kg of cannabis in four suitcases belonging to two foreign passengers who were transiting to a third country. Both were convicted of drug smuggling and sentenced to eight and four years in prison, with fines and deportation.

reports.title: Aleppo anti-narcotics seize 800 kg of hashish
reports.summary: The anti-narcotics branch in Aleppo arrested two Lebanese nationals and seized about 800 kilograms of hashish and 200,000 narcotic pills. The head of the Drug Enforcement Administration said the men were trying to smuggle the shipment and that the drugs would be destroyed. It was one of the largest cannabis seizures reported since the fall of Assad.

reports.title: Syria's new government says the drug factories are gone
reports.summary: Six months after the fall of Bashar al-Assad, the interior minister, Anas Khattab, said every Captagon laboratory in the country had been dismantled. In the weeks after the collapse the security forces had destroyed about 100 million pills and about 15 tonnes of hashish. He named treatment and rehabilitation of addicts as the next priority.

reports.title: Timor-Leste's 2022 cannabis case reaches court after nearly three years
reports.summary: The Dili court began the pre-trial debate in the case against 13 defendants charged after the 12 August 2022 raids; nine appeared and four were abroad. The 2022 seizure included hashish, hashish chocolate and 0.50 g of methamphetamine, with $4,139.25 in cash. Witnesses described the intelligence-led raids and disputed who had detained the first five suspects.

reports.title: Laos seizes 86 kg of cannabis at Wattay airport
reports.summary: Three Malaysians aged 25 to 29 were arrested at Wattay International Airport in Vientiane with 86 kg of cannabis in 103 packages, concealed in suitcases and bound for Germany. The case was one of the few cannabis-specific airport seizures reported in 2025.

reports.title: Bhutan uproots wild cannabis nationwide
reports.summary: The Royal Bhutan Police began a nationwide cannabis uprooting campaign across all twenty dzongkhags in May 2025, starting with Thimphu. The force reported 13.15 kg of cannabis leaves, 1.26 kg of hashish and 337 plants seized in 2024, and 225 cannabis-abuse cases against 197 in 2023. The campaign was enforcement, not a change in the law.

reports.title: Taliban court gives hashish traffickers prison and lashes
reports.summary: A Taliban court sentences eleven people for trafficking hashish and narcotic tablets to between seven months and three and a half years in prison, plus ten to thirty-nine lashes.[@1]

reports.title: Kiunga police seize 18 kg of marijuana sent by mail
reports.summary: Police in Kiunga, Western Province, arrested two men from Western Highlands after finding about 18 kg of dried marijuana in two boxes at Rubber Corner. The boxes had been sent by Mail Express from Mount Hagen via Port Moresby; police put the street value at K90,000–100,000. Both were charged under section 3(1) of the Dangerous Drugs Act.

reports.title: Qatar customs find 6 kg of hashish in car parts
reports.summary: Customs officers at Hamad International Airport found 6 kilograms of hashish and 1 kilogram of heroin hidden in automotive spare parts in a passenger's luggage. The General Authority of Customs said the drugs were seized and legal proceedings began. The seizure was announced on 23 May 2025.

reports.title: Thailand warns tourists against taking cannabis out of the country
reports.summary: As cases of travellers smuggling cannabis rose, the health minister, Somsak Thepsutin, said it was against Thai law to take cannabis out of the country without permission from the authorities, and that shops would soon be allowed to sell only to customers with a prescription. In March 375 kg had been seized in 22 suitcases at Samui airport and 13 foreigners arrested.

reports.title: Thai cannabis turns Kathmandu airport into a transit route
reports.summary: In the year to mid-April 2025, police seized 114.8 kg of cannabis at Tribhuvan International Airport, up from 540 grams the year before and 36 grams in 2022. Most came in suitcases on flights from Thailand, where legalisation had made strong indoor-grown cannabis easy to buy, and investigators said the destination was India.

reports.title: Türkiye destroys 7.5 million cannabis plants in Diyarbakır
reports.summary: Governor-led teams raided cannabis fields in seven districts of Diyarbakır with 2,212 personnel, a helicopter and drones, destroying 7,543,818 cannabis and skunk plants. The governor's office said the plants could have produced 174 tonnes of hashish, and eight people were detained. The operation was one of the largest in the southeast, where most illegal cannabis cultivation is found.

reports.title: Kiribati police find a second cannabis plantation in Tarawa
reports.summary: Police found a cannabis plantation about two metres high near the clinic at Takoronga, Tarawa, arrested and cautioned a suspect, and described it as the second drug bust of 2025. The first was at Abatao on 28 April.

reports.title: Dushanbe police seize 16 kg of hashish and opium from a delivery group
reports.summary: Police stopped three men transporting 16 kg of hashish and opium into Dushanbe and opened a case under part 4 of Article 200, the especially-large supply offence. The men were held in custody while police looked for their supply chain. The offence carries 12–20 years in prison.

reports.title: Kiribati police find a two-metre cannabis plant at Abatao
reports.summary: Police found a cannabis plant almost two metres high at Abatao, Tarawa, arrested a suspect and asked the public for information. It was the first cannabis raid reported in 2025.

reports.title: A Monaco court convicts a pensioner over 15 g of cannabis and CBD products
reports.summary: A Monegasque man born in 1956, with a clean record, was tried for possession and use of narcotics after a search of his home found 15.62 g of cannabis, a CBD spray and CBD chewing gum. The prosecutor cited a ministerial order banning cannabis and its derivatives, including CBD, even at low THC levels, and asked for three months suspended.

reports.title: Tripoli court jails a man for life over imported cannabis seeds
reports.summary: The Tripoli Criminal Court sentenced a man to life imprisonment for importing cannabis seeds with customs documents that falsely described the goods. It fined him 40,000 dinars and permanently stripped him of his civil rights. The charge was importing the seeds, not growing plants.

reports.title: Brunei records 777 drug arrests as meth seizures surge
reports.summary: Brunei recorded 777 drug arrests in 2024, up from 711 in 2023; 641 were men, 136 women, and 645 were locals. Methamphetamine seizures rose above 40 kg, while UNODC recorded 2.6 kg of herbal cannabis seized against 6.3 kg in 2023. No cannabis-specific arrest count was published.

reports.title: Palestinian prosecutors handled 1,396 drug cases in 2024
reports.summary: The Palestinian Public Prosecution's 2024 annual report said it opened investigations into 1,396 drug cases and resolved 97% of them. The report covers the areas under PA jurisdiction; Gaza's courts were outside the PA system and largely closed by the war.

reports.title: Gendarmes seize 350 kg at Ihosy after traffickers flee
reports.summary: Gendarmes and soldiers seized 350.06 kg of cannabis in 25 sacks at Sahambano forest, Ihosy, after traffickers opened fire and fled. Local police seized another 52 kg. No arrests were reported.

reports.title: Cameroon's gendarmes find 50 sacks of cannabis in a soap lorry
reports.summary: Gendarmes of the Njimom brigade stopped a lorry at the Manki checkpoint in the Noun department of the West region and found 50 sacks of cannabis hidden among cartons of soap. The driver and two other men were detained, and the defence ministry said they and the cargo would be handed to the courts.

reports.title: CNB finds 6.9 kg of cannabis in a Cavenagh Road flat
reports.summary: On 19 March 2025 narcotics officers forced entry to a private flat near Cavenagh Road and found about 6,885 g of cannabis in the bedroom where a 26-year-old Singaporean man was arrested.[@1] They also seized 'Ice', ketamine, Ecstasy, LSD stamps and GHB, and a further 25 g of cannabis in his car.[@1] CNB valued the cannabis at more than S$184,000 and said it could feed about 1,040 abusers for a…

reports.title: Turkmen border guards find 15 kg of Afghan heroin with a shepherd
reports.summary: Border guards on the Afghan frontier in Mary region found 15 kg of heroin hidden in a shepherd's animal feed during a search on 13 March 2025. The shepherd said he was to move the drugs to Ahal and Dashoguz regions and refused to name his accomplices. The case was reported on 27 March; it involved heroin, not cannabis, and showed the border service's role in interdicting Afghan opiates.

reports.title: Choiseul police charge a grower under both cannabis offences
reports.summary: Police at Taro in Choiseul arrested a 27-year-old man on 6 March 2025 and charged him with growing prohibited plants under section 8(a) and possessing a dangerous drug under section 8(b) of the Dangerous Drugs Act. Officers uprooted his plants and found cannabis on him at the arrest. The case shows both limbs of the 1941 law being used against a small grower.

reports.title: Niger's anti-drug office seizes cannabis hidden in peanuts
reports.summary: The Konni unit of the anti-drug office OCRTIS found 80 bricks of cannabis weighing 72.325 kg in sacks of peanuts at the Tchérassa checkpoint. The load had come from Kalmalo in Nigeria and was bound for Dan Issa and Maradi. Three people were arrested for international trafficking of high-risk drugs.

reports.title: French Polynesia's Matai Rorofai operation destroys 7,419 plants
reports.summary: A two-week operation across the territory ended with 7,419 cannabis plants destroyed, 17.2 kg of herb, 31.57 g of ice and 80 ecstasy tablets seized, and 15.7 million XFP in assets. Police implicated 395 people and held 45 in custody. It was an enforcement operation, not a change in the law.

reports.title: Syria's new border force finds hashish factories on the Lebanese border
reports.summary: The commander of Syria's western border region said his forces had found numerous hashish farms, warehouses and processing and packing workshops during a sweep of villages along the Lebanese border. He said the area had been the economic artery of armed smuggling gangs and that the former regime had turned the border into a drug corridor.

reports.title: Tajikistan's 2024 drug haul falls as synthetics take over
reports.summary: The Drug Control Agency reported that law enforcement seized about 4.3 tonnes of drugs in 2024, 901 kg less than in 2023. Seizures of plant-based drugs fell by more than 900 kg, while psychotropic substances rose to 101 kg, 59% more than the year before. The agency said traffickers were shifting from cannabis and opium toward methamphetamine and other synthetics.

reports.title: Malaysia jails three men for life over 707 g of cannabis
reports.summary: The Kuala Lumpur High Court sentenced a former air steward and two other men to life imprisonment and 18 strokes of the cane for trafficking 707.05 g of cannabis and cultivating plants. The trafficking charge carried 12 strokes and the cultivation charge six, to run concurrently from their arrest in December 2021.

reports.title: Jordan seizes three tonnes of hashish in 2024
reports.summary: The Anti-Narcotics Department reported 25,260 drug cases involving 38,782 people in 2024. It seized 3,000 kg of hashish, 262 kg of marijuana and 27.5 million Captagon pills, and 744 people entered rehabilitation. The figures cover all drugs, not cannabis alone.

reports.title: Tonga police arrest six people with small amounts of cannabis and methamphetamine
reports.summary: In two raids on a bush allotment at Hauloto on 2 and 6 January 2025, Tonga Police arrested six people. In the first they seized 21 packs of cannabis weighing 8.17 g and five packs of methamphetamine; in the second, two packs of cannabis weighing 1.54 g and 27 packs of methamphetamine.

reports.title: Libya's anti-narcotics agency reports a pill-heavy 2024
reports.summary: The eastern-based Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Agency reported seizing 8,051,317 pills, 759.6 kg of cocaine and 1.7 kg of heroin in 2024, with a total value of about 620 million dinars. It also listed 2,073 arrests and just 951 grams of hashish. Pills and cocaine dominated the published haul.

reports.title: Oman police seize 75 kg of mixed drugs smuggled by sea
reports.summary: The Royal Oman Police arrested two people and seized more than 75 kilograms of drugs, including crystal meth, hashish, marijuana and psychotropic tablets, in a shipment smuggled by sea, the force said on 29 December 2024. The statement did not split the haul by drug or name the vessel's origin. It showed cannabis resin and herb moving alongside methamphetamine and tablets in the same shipment.

reports.title: Vietnam breaks up a crypto-paid cannabis ring and seizes 550 kg
reports.summary: Anti-narcotics police announced on 20 December 2024 that they had broken up a cannabis ring that took payment through unverified bank accounts and cryptocurrency. Ten people were arrested and 550 kg of dried cannabis and 10 kg of resin were seized, along with packaging disguised as tea and food. The ringleader told police he had arranged seven shipments, about two tonnes, in two months.

reports.title: Bolivia reports 1,269 tonnes of marijuana seized in four years
reports.summary: Government minister Eduardo Del Castillo reported that the anti-narcotics force Felcn had seized about 1,269 tonnes of marijuana and 139 tonnes of cocaine between November 2020 and December 2024, and that 13,359 people had been arrested for drug trafficking in that time.

reports.title: Dubai jails a cannabis supplier for life over 193 grams
reports.summary: Dubai's criminal court sentenced a 35-year-old Bangladeshi man to life in prison, 25 years under UAE law, for trafficking cannabis after police found 193.13 grams in his flat and WhatsApp messages about sales. He had been caught in a sting in Al Nahda after a Sudanese buyer led investigators to him.

reports.title: Congo gendarmes link a cannabis seizure to an agriculture official
reports.summary: An official report described the arrest in Owando of a young adult carrying 52 wrapped cannabis portions, followed by a search of an agriculture official's home where more cannabis and an elephant tusk were found. The suspects were presented to the prosecutor. The report, dated 20 November, still cited the colonial-era 1916 poisonous-substances law as a basis for cannabis enforcement.

reports.title: Uzbekistan says drug crime doubled in five years
reports.summary: The director of the National Centre for Drug Control said drug offences had doubled between 2019 and 2024, drug seizures rose 8.5 times and synthetic-drug seizures 400 times. He warned that 'pharmacy drug addiction' was spreading among young people and called for regional cooperation. The figures cover all drugs, not cannabis alone.

reports.title: Kazakhstan's 2024 cannabis sweep finds 21.5 tonnes of drugs
reports.summary: The interior ministry's Karasora operation ran from 1 June to 31 October 2024 and recorded 1,607 drug crimes: 799 sales, 245 cultivation and 194 possession. Police seized 21.5 tonnes of drugs, including about 4.5 tonnes of marijuana, more than 200 kg of hashish and 16 tonnes of cannabis plants, and destroyed more than 100 tonnes of wild cannabis on 380 hectares in the Shu district.

reports.title: Tabubil court jails a man six years for 4.5 kg of marijuana
reports.summary: The Tabubil District Court sentenced Ipark Amlat, 38, to six years' hard labour for possessing 4.5 kg of marijuana, charged under section 3(1)(d) of the Dangerous Drugs Act. He had been arrested on 12 October 2024 and pleaded guilty; 25 days in pre-trial custody were deducted. Police put the street value at K20,000–30,000.

reports.title: Bangui police destroy cannabis seized along the river and in markets
reports.summary: The anti-drug office destroyed seized cannabis and other products after operations along the Oubangui river, in Boy-Rabe and at Combattant market. Radio Ndeke Luka reported that the seizures took place from 14 to 20 October, before the destruction on 5 November.

reports.title: Oman police seize 30 kg of hashish in South Al Batinah
reports.summary: The Royal Oman Police arrested one person in South Al Batinah after finding more than 30 kilograms of hashish, the force said on 21 October 2024. It gave no origin, destination or estimated value for the resin. The case was one of the larger single cannabis seizures reported in Oman that year.

reports.title: Bishkek police find 27 kg of marijuana packed for sale
reports.summary: After a man handed hashish to police in Bishkek on 3 September 2024, investigators traced a house in Bash-Kara-Suu, Alamedin district, where they detained a 37-year-old man and woman. A search found 1,150 packets of cannabis straw weighing 26.907 kg in total, which the man said were sold at 2,000 som each, about 2.5 million som. The case was opened under the supply article of the Criminal Code.

reports.title: Taiwan breaks its record for cannabis plants seized in one case
reports.summary: Prosecutors announced on 15 October 2024 that raids in Hsinchu in May had found 5,659 cannabis plants and 1,666 seeds across two indoor farms, with a street value estimated at more than NT$20 billion. Police said the farms belonged to the same group and charged 11 people, including an alleged organised-crime figure. It was the largest cannabis cultivation case by plant count in Taiwan's history.

reports.title: A drone from Iran brings marijuana over the Araz
reports.summary: Border guards in the Horadiz sector intercepted an unmanned aerial device flying from Iran and found 19.7 kg of marijuana and 1,500 methadone tablets, the State Border Service reported. It was one of a series of drone-borne drug shipments along the Araz river border in 2024 and 2025, alongside marijuana hidden in lorries and boats.

reports.title: Customs finds 500 kg of cannabis hidden in a soybean shipment
reports.summary: Customs seized about 500 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds, worth about HK$130 million, from a sea container declared as carrying soy beans from Canada at Kwai Chung on 27 September 2024. Officers found the buds in 83 bags, then arrested two men and one woman aged 44 to 55 after a controlled delivery. The case showed smugglers using ordinary food cargoes to move cannabis into Hong Kong.

reports.title: Guyana's attorney general tells police not to lock people up for small amounts
reports.summary: After police in Matthew's Ridge held a man found with 4.2 g of marijuana, Attorney General Anil Nandlall said the detention misapplied the amended drug law. Because a court cannot impose prison for possessing up to 30 g, he said, the police cannot detain a person for it before trial and bail must be granted; they should charge the person and bring them before a magistrate.

reports.title: Police seize 17 kg of cannabis plants in Ulaanbaatar
reports.summary: Police stopped two men aged 32 and 33 in Ulaanbaatar’s Songinokhairkhan district on 12 September 2024 with about 17 kg of cannabis plants. The case was cited under Article 20.7 of the Criminal Code; no verdict was reported. It was one of the few cannabis-specific seizures reported that year.

reports.title: Marshall Islands charges a Majuro man after a marijuana and meth search
reports.summary: Elai Aiseia, 40, was charged in August 2024 with unlawful possession and sale of prohibited drugs and unlawful possession of marijuana after police searched his Uliga home. The search followed a driving-under-the-influence arrest in May, when the driver told police he had bought crack cocaine from Aiseia. Officers found marijuana in bags and containers, methamphetamine, crack and $1,109 in cash.

reports.title: Bahrain finds hashish soaked into posted fabric
reports.summary: Police arrested a 32-year-old baker at his home on 27 August 2024 after a parcel of fabric soaked in hashish arrived in Bahrain by post. Officers found bags bearing traces of cannabis, BHD1,516.925 and SAR635 in cash; prosecutors said he was part of a wider group using concealed shipments. The case was before the courts in April 2025, with a verdict expected on 29 April.

reports.title: Dushanbe police seize 50 kg of hashish from a transnational group
reports.summary: Police in Dushanbe's Shohmansur district arrested two men from Istravshan with 50 kg of hashish. A criminal case was opened under Article 200 of the Criminal Code, which can carry up to 20 years for especially large supply. The police said they were still looking for other members of the group.

reports.title: Auki police uproot nearly 200 cannabis plants after a village tip-off
reports.summary: On 20 August 2024 police in Auki uprooted nearly 200 marijuana plants near Ngadefiu village in Central Kwara'ae, Malaita. Community leaders had helped the police, and the alleged owner ran off before officers arrived; no arrest was reported. The provincial commander praised the village for acting against cultivation.

reports.title: Transnistrian police uncover 64 cannabis plants in Bender garden
reports.summary: During the annual Mak-2024 anti-drug operation, militia officers in the city of Bender raided a residential plot and discovered 64 two-metre-tall cannabis plants cultivated alongside dried marijuana.

reports.title: Marshall Islands police find marijuana in a raid on the national jail
reports.summary: Majuro Atoll Local Police searched the national police jail in Uliga on 3 August 2024 and found marijuana, crystal meth, cash, mobile phones and alcohol in prisoners' cells. The raid followed a sting in which an inmate sold methamphetamine to a police informant.

reports.title: Customs finds 15 kg of cannabis in a suitcase at Velana airport
reports.summary: Officers found more than 15 kg of cannabis in the luggage of a 44-year-old Malaysian man who arrived on flight EK656 on 27 July 2024. Police put the street value at MVR 12.3 million and called it the largest single cannabis seizure of the year; a controlled delivery led to a second arrest, of a 41-year-old Malaysian man.

reports.title: Britain and Thailand join forces against cannabis couriers
reports.summary: A UK-led operation with Thai customs began in July 2024 to stop cannabis carried or posted from Thailand to Britain. By April 2025 more than 50 British nationals had been arrested in Thailand, Thai customs had intercepted over 800 smugglers and nine tonnes of cannabis since October 2024, and cannabis posted to Britain had fallen by 90 per cent in the first quarter of 2025.

reports.title: Malagasy gendarmes uproot ten hectares of cannabis in a protected area
reports.summary: In an operation from 4 to 15 July in the protected zone of Mount Tsaratanàna, in Ambanja district, twenty gendarmes and four agents of Madagascar National Parks uprooted about 600,000 cannabis plants on ten hectares and burned 950 kg of dried cannabis. The growers fled as the patrols arrived and no one was arrested.

reports.title: North Hamgyong reports a 40% rise in drug crime and orders a summer crackdown
reports.summary: The provincial security bureau told the party committee in early July 2024 that drug offences in North Hamgyong had risen 40% from a year earlier, with more than 900 cases in Chongjin in the first half of the year. The committee made July and August an intensive crackdown and said smuggling drugs to China should draw heavier sentences, up to death.

reports.title: São Tomé police raid cannabis fields and sales points, arresting nine
reports.summary: Police’s Operation 971 targeted cannabis fields and sales points across São Tomé and Príncipe in July 2024, according to a later account of the operation.[@1] Seven men and two women, all São Toméan, were detained and brought for an initial judicial hearing.[@1] The operation involved the prison and social reintegration service and the state leaders’ protection unit alongside the judicial…

reports.title: Kyrgyzstan burns 85 tonnes of wild cannabis
reports.summary: In July 2024 the drug-control service mapped 627 hectares of wild cannabis and sent 90 brigades to cut and burn it. The service reported more than 85 tonnes destroyed, including 27 tonnes in Chuy region, 17 tonnes in Issyk-Kul and Naryn, 15 tonnes in Bishkek and smaller amounts in the south. The operation was part of the annual Kara-kuurai eradication campaign.

reports.title: Marib forces seize 190 kg of hashish bound for Houthi areas
reports.summary: Security forces in Marib stopped a truck carrying 190 kg of hashish at a checkpoint and said it was being smuggled into Houthi-controlled territory. The head of Marib's drug-control department, Abdul Razzaq al-Ruwaifi, said the shipment and the accused were handed to the prosecution. The seizure was announced by the official Saba news agency and reported by Yemen Monitor.

reports.title: Palau seizes 182 cannabis plants in Peleliu
reports.summary: Police seized 182 cannabis plants, $31,600 in cash, seeds, joints, scales and a ledger in Peleliu; Anna Gotlob was charged on 4 July 2024. Peleliu had been raided repeatedly since 2019, showing that local cultivation persisted despite the crackdowns.

reports.title: Armenia stops bringing criminal cases for small plant-based possession
reports.summary: In 2024 prosecutors stopped opening criminal cases for small amounts of plant-based drugs, cannabis included, when there was no evidence of sale, and sent the files for an administrative fine instead. Drug crimes fell from 5,070 in 2023 to 3,639 in 2024, while administrative drug offences rose from 387 to 633.

reports.title: Illicit small-scale growing still dwarfs the legal sector
reports.summary: Fieldwork in 2022–2024 found Zimbabwe's illicit cannabis sector still far larger than the new legal one in estimated output and significance to people's livelihoods.[@1] Mutoko in the north-east and Binga in the north-west were known for small-scale illicit cultivation, with local supply complemented by imports from Malawi, South Africa and Mozambique.[@1] Binga and Chiredzi were chosen for…

reports.title: Micronesia finds probable cause in a 183-gram mailed-cannabis case
reports.summary: In FSM v. Ehsa, customs found 183 g of marijuana joints in a parcel addressed to a Pohnpei post office box. The court upheld probable cause under the possession and trafficking provisions and rejected search and entrapment arguments at the preliminary stage. The final disposition was not traced.

reports.title: South Korea's 2023 drug arrests pass 20,000 for the first time
reports.summary: The prosecution service's yearly report recorded 27,611 people caught for drug offences in 2023, half as many again as the 18,395 of 2022. Teenagers numbered 1,477, three times the year before, and people in their twenties 8,368. The report as published did not break the figures down by drug.

reports.title: Timor-Leste's drug police still send samples to Portugal for confirmatory testing
reports.summary: The scientific police said they lacked staff and equipment to confirm whether seized material was a controlled drug, so samples went to Portugal's judicial police and results took about two weeks. They described initial testing in Dili and a 2022 cannabis case that was still in court. The statement points to the laboratory gap the 2012 UN assessment had already identified.

reports.title: Brunei arrests 27 in a Tutong drug sweep
reports.summary: Police arrested 27 people in Operasi Ursa Heal in Tutong on 16 and 19 June 2024, seizing 75.29 g of syabu and 37.21 g of cannabis. The operation was one of the year's street-level enforcement actions and did not change the law.

reports.title: A Philippine court convicts four police for a drug-war killing
reports.summary: A Caloocan court found four policemen guilty of homicide for killing Luis and Gabriel Bonifacio during a September 2016 drug raid. The officers were sentenced to up to ten years in prison and ordered to pay damages to the family. It was only the fourth known conviction of police for a drug-war killing, out of thousands of deaths.

reports.title: A Tahiti father who grew cannabis for his epileptic son is acquitted
reports.summary: The court in Papeete acquitted a father prosecuted for two years over about a hundred plants grown in Taravao to make oil for his son; the prosecutor had asked it to waive punishment. Growing for therapy remained prohibited.

reports.title: Lebanon seizes 6.4 kg of hashish at Beirut airport
reports.summary: Customs seized 6.416 kg of hashish at Beirut airport from an Egyptian traveller, hidden in a shipping suitcase and bound for an Arab country. The case was one of the few cannabis-specific seizures reported in 2024.

reports.title: Nauru fines two adults after a one-gram cannabis case
reports.summary: Two adults received fines of A$1,500 each, community service and one year’s probation after pleading guilty in a one-gram cannabis case. A teenager received a A$200 fine and one month’s community service, with no conviction recorded.[@1] The magistrate considered imprisonment disproportionate for the adults, months before parliament introduced mandatory custody for possession.[@1,2]

reports.title: Fiji’s appeal court cuts two cannabis growers’ prison terms by four years
reports.summary: Waisake Kaloulia’s nineteen-year cannabis cultivation sentence was reduced to fifteen years, and Kaminieli Naqeleca’s eighteen years to fourteen. The Court of Appeal applied its newer plant-count and role guidelines to the men’s older case, involving a remote plantation with at least 208 whole plants confirmed in the analyst’s report.

reports.title: Vanuatu suspends a five-plant sentence after months already spent in custody
reports.summary: A first offender who grew five cannabis plants weighing 15.5 grams received a suspended sentence, sixty hours of community work and six months’ supervision.[@1] Brightly Kaiding had already spent three months and two days in custody before bail, which the court deducted from a nine-month term, leaving five months and twenty-eight days suspended for two years.[@1] The court treated the grow…

reports.title: Gibraltar fines and disqualifies a driver after a positive cannabis test
reports.summary: A driver was fined £250 and disqualified for eight months after testing at not less than 3.8 micrograms of THC per litre of blood. Police had stopped his erratically driven car in November 2023.

reports.title: Police seize 19 kg of drugs in the first months of 2024
reports.summary: Police said 56 operations had seized about 19 kg of drugs by mid-May 2024, with a street value of MVR 104 million. They had arrested 260 Maldivians and 16 foreigners, opened 257 drug cases, sent 95 to the Prosecutor General and reported shutting five drug networks. The figures covered all drugs, not cannabis alone.

reports.title: Isle of Man court fines a woman for half a gram of cannabis
reports.summary: A woman received a £300 fine and £125 costs for possessing half a gram of cannabis. The reported case shows that a small personal quantity can still lead to a court penalty alongside the island's referral options for eligible offenders.

reports.title: Nauru police record 175 offences in the first quarter
reports.summary: Police recorded 175 crime offences in the first quarter of 2024 across categories including illicit drug use and possession, but published no drug-specific breakdown. The figure covers all crime, not cannabis alone.

reports.title: Mozambique's top court cuts a cannabis seller's sentence to six years
reports.summary: The Supreme Court reduced Raiva Rafael Meponda's seventeen-year sentence to six years and a 30,000-metical fine after police found 590 grams of cannabis in 232 portions at his Maputo home. The judges rejected his personal-use argument but treated his simple, direct sales without an organisation as small-scale trafficking.

reports.title: Qatar police arrest two men in a drug-trafficking raid
reports.summary: The Ministry of Interior published video of a surveillance operation that ended with a car chase and the arrest of two men accused of trafficking drugs. Officers searched the men and their vehicles and said they found illegal items, but the announcement gave no quantity or charge. The ministry did not say what happened to the men after the arrest.

reports.title: A new wave of cannabis arrests hits young Tunisians
reports.summary: An investigation published on 18 March 2024 found cannabis users facing random street stops, house raids, phone searches and pre-trial detention, with lawyers saying the repression was the worst since Ben Ali. People were held for carrying rolling papers or filters, and activists said prosecutors treated small users as dealers.

reports.title: Bolikhamxay police find more than 800 kg of cannabis
reports.summary: Lao media reported on 26 March 2024 that a couple had been arrested in Bolikhamxay with more than 800 kg of cannabis and nearly 300 amphetamine pills. The same report described 1,000 kg of crystal meth seized in Xayaboury and 166 kg in Bokeo. It gave no charge, court date or sentence for the cannabis case.

reports.title: Manila port raid finds kush, hash and vape oil in one shipment
reports.summary: PDEA, Customs and the PNP Maritime Group seized 278.32 kg of marijuana kush, 2.36 litres of liquid marijuana in vape cartridges and 880.25 grams of hash at the Manila International Container Port. The same operation found 1.06 kg of dried mushroom.

reports.title: Indonesia burns seven tonnes of ripe cannabis in Aceh
reports.summary: BNN destroyed about seven tonnes wet weight of mostly ready-to-harvest cannabis on four hectares in Aceh Besar, roughly 20,000 plants, on 6 March 2024. Days earlier it had seized 200 kg of dried cannabis and arrested a suspect in the same district. The fields were found with monitoring by the national research agency (BRIN) and the geospatial agency (BIG).

reports.title: Sri Lanka says police can arrest unauthorised holders of Ayurvedic cannabis
reports.summary: After Yukthiya raids on Ayurvedic practitioners, the Ayurveda Commissioner General said only registered institutions and pharmacies may hold cannabis medicines, that prescriptions are required, and that police may prosecute possession outside those conditions. The statement followed complaints that the crackdown had treated traditional medicines as recreational drugs.

reports.title: Bosnia’s state police report cannabis seizures and drug-trafficking cases
reports.summary: SIPA reported 78.904 kg of marijuana/skank and 126 cannabis plants seized during 2023. Its all-drug trafficking work covered 68 cases and sixteen reports to prosecutors concerning 32 people, plus a supplementary report concerning three people.

reports.title: Serbia’s top court keeps three years for 372 grams of personal cannabis
reports.summary: The Supreme Court upheld Senad Makaji’s three-year prison sentence for holding about 372 grams of cannabis, even though it was for his own use. An appeal had increased his original thirteen-month sentence by applying the large-quantity offence introduced in 2019.

reports.title: Faroese customs find 24 kg of hashish in a ferry passenger’s car
reports.summary: Customs found 24 kg of hashish in a car arriving on Norrøna. Police arrested two people and charged them under Penal Code § 191; the following day a court remanded them for four weeks.

reports.title: Thai cannabis drinks slip into Vientiane shops
reports.summary: Radio Free Asia reported in January 2024 that Thai drinks containing up to 0.2% THC were on sale in Vientiane markets, despite Laos's ban. A Vientiane police officer said only cannabis products authorised by the Ministry of Health for medical use were allowed and that police confiscated illegal products.

reports.title: Sri Lanka launches Operation Yukthiya against drug suspects
reports.summary: Acting Inspector General Deshabandu Tennekoon, backed by Public Security Minister Tiran Alles, launched a nationwide anti-drug operation on 17 December that arrested at least a thousand people a day in its first weeks.

reports.title: Sana'a court hands five death sentences in a 994 kg hashish case
reports.summary: The Specialized Criminal Court in Sana'a sentenced 32 defendants in a hashish-trafficking case: five to death, 12 to 25 years and 15 to five years. The court ordered 994 kg of hashish destroyed and confiscated property; in a separate case that day, one man got five years and two others 25 years for possessing a block of hashish.

reports.title: Cuba's Supreme Court reports 689 people sanctioned for drugs
reports.summary: The head of the Supreme Court's criminal chamber said on state television that courts had sanctioned 689 people linked to drug trafficking so far that year, 92% with prison sentences. These totals cover drugs generally, not cannabis alone. Authorities separately reported 77 cases of marihuana growing.

reports.title: Saied orders a harder drug crackdown
reports.summary: On 6 November 2023 President Kais Saied met the interior minister, the national guard commander and the director general of national security and called for more patrols and a tougher fight against drugs. The meeting followed similar remarks on 26 October. Lawyers later linked the instructions to the arrest wave of 2024.

reports.title: A fifth of Iraqi Kurdistan's prisoners are held for drugs
reports.summary: The regional government reported that 1,097 of its 5,283 prisoners were serving sentences for narcotics, 617 of them for use and 480 for trafficking, in prisons holding about three times their capacity. Arrests had risen from 142 in 2014 to 2,017 in 2022.

reports.title: The leader of Namibia's cannabis challenge is jailed for possession
reports.summary: Brian Jaftha, who had brought the constitutional case against the cannabis ban, was sentenced to two years in prison for possession, about five years after his arrest. He said the plant material was never tested and that the investigating officer had died and could not be cross-examined. His lawyer in the constitutional case said the sentence did not end that challenge.

reports.title: Somaliland police report a cannabis-cultivation arrest
reports.summary: Somaliland police reported arresting a man accused of growing cannabis in the yard of a house he owned in Hargeisa’s Ga’an Libaah district.[@1] The published account said traffic police worked with the district station; it reported an arrest and allegation, with no conviction or sentence.[@1]

reports.title: Qatar's customs find 87 kg of hashish in bales of animal feed
reports.summary: Customs officers at Hamad Port announced that they had found about 87.5 kilograms of hashish packed among stacks of hay in a container declared as animal feed.

reports.title: Gaza military courts hand down two more drug death sentences
reports.summary: Gaza's military appeal and permanent courts sentenced two men to death and eight to life imprisonment in a batch of drug cases. One man was convicted of repeated trafficking under article 29 of the 2013 drug law; the other of importing drugs for trafficking under article 28.

reports.title: A Los Santos grower gets 80 months for 12 plants
reports.summary: A court sentenced a man to 80 months in prison for cultivation and custody of marijuana seeds and plants under article 314 of the Penal Code, after police found 12 plants and 279 seeds in Los Santos.

reports.title: Hong Kong jails a traveller in its first CBD imprisonment case
reports.summary: A traveller received two months overall after convictions for possessing CBD, possessing ketamine and having injection equipment.[@1] Officers had found two personal-care bottles containing about 5 g of CBD, about 2.2 g of ketamine and ten syringes after her arrival from the United States in March.

reports.title: Gaza court again sentences a drug trafficker to death
reports.summary: Gaza's Supreme Criminal Chamber sentenced a 30-year-old man to death by hanging for possessing and trafficking narcotics to Israel. PCHR called it the first death sentence of 2023 and said the number issued since 1994 had reached 281, including 251 in Gaza.

reports.title: World Cup visitors are warned that Qatar arrests for the smallest amounts
reports.summary: Ahead of the football World Cup, a news agency's guide for fans described Qatar as one of the most restrictive countries in the world on drugs: cannabis is prohibited, as are some common medicines; bags and passengers are scanned at Hamad International Airport, and travellers carrying even very small quantities have been arrested. Smuggling charges can carry the death penalty.

reports.title: Gaza court sentences a hashish dealer to death
reports.summary: Gaza's Grand Criminal Court sentenced a man to death by hanging for possessing hashish and 'happy pills' with intent to traffic, a repeat offence. SHAMS said the PA's 2018 drug law did not provide death; PCHR later said Gaza's 2013 law did. It was the first death sentence by that court in a drug case.

reports.title: Cabo Verde seizes 717 kg of cannabis in Ribeira Grande
reports.summary: The Judicial Police seized about 717 kg of cannabis in Tronco, Ribeira Grande de Santiago, during field checks of cannabis-growing areas; 17 kg was ready to enter the market.[@1] A 38-year-old local man was detained outside flagrante delicto, and a court imposed preventive detention, the harshest pre-trial measure.[@1] All seized drugs were incinerated on site after weighing.[@1]

reports.title: Timor-Leste arrests nine in a Dili drug operation involving cannabis
reports.summary: Police and intelligence officers arrested nine suspects in Dili on 11–12 August; TATOLI reported seizures including suspected cannabis and methamphetamine.[@1] The district court imposed identity-and-residence declarations and periodic reporting, a decision later challenged publicly by a student movement.[@2] Justice Minister Tiago Amaral Sarmento also called for stronger penalties and…

reports.title: Bahrain sentences a hashish smuggler to death over 50 kg from Iran
reports.summary: The High Criminal Court sentenced a Bahraini man to death on 19 July 2022 for importing and possessing 50 kg of hashish with intent to distribute; prosecutors said the shipment came from Iran and the intelligence dated from March. On appeal the sentence became life imprisonment, and the Court of Cassation upheld the life term on 24 July 2023.

reports.title: Timor-Leste police seize live cannabis seedlings from Ireland
reports.summary: Police and customs seized a package of live cannabis seedlings during maritime cargo checks on 1 June, the national police reported.[@1] Officers detained a 43-year-old who came to collect it; police said relatives had sent the parcel from Ireland and that examination of its quantity was continuing.[@1] The suspect was referred for an initial court hearing on 3 June.[@1]

reports.title: Bor court gives five young men prison terms and fines five over bhang
reports.summary: A Bor court sentenced ten men aged eighteen to twenty-two after police found them smoking bhang during a night patrol. According to the state police commissioner, one received a year in prison, four received six months, and five were fined 50,000 South Sudanese pounds each.[@1] Police also arrested a supplier; the report did not state how much cannabis each young man held.[@1]

reports.title: Tanzania upholds thirty years for growing cannabis but drops a possession count
reports.summary: Tanzania's Court of Appeal upheld Hamis Muhibu Abdallah's thirty-year sentence for cultivating cannabis after police found 535 plants on a farm.[@1] It quashed a separate possession conviction because the uprooted plants proved cultivation, not the additional possession offence charged.[@1] His confession, though retracted, was supported by other evidence linking him to the field, so the…

reports.title: Central African Republic police seize cannabis during a security operation
reports.summary: A joint security operation in Ouandago had led to eleven arrests and the seizure of eleven homemade weapons and over ten kilograms of cannabis, MINUSCA reported. The operation responded to abuses by a self-defence group; the figures were a mid-operation report.

reports.title: Libya's unity government rebuilds the anti-narcotics agency
reports.summary: The Tripoli-based Government of National Unity organised a new Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Agency with its headquarters in Tripoli and branches to be opened by the interior minister. The agency was given powers over cultivation, trafficking and use, treatment and rehabilitation, and its own budget, including half of the assets confiscated in drug cases.

reports.title: Kiribati fines a man A$250 for keeping one cannabis plant
reports.summary: A man who kept a small cannabis plant belonging to his late half-brother received a A$250 fine after pleading guilty to possession. Chief Justice William Hastings found no evidence of use or dealing and treated the case as less serious than the earlier fisheries officer’s cannabis offence.[@1] Failure to pay by the end of December would bring one month in prison.[@1]

reports.title: An American teacher gets 14 years in Russia for medical cannabis
reports.summary: Customs officers at Sheremetyevo airport found about 17 grams of cannabis in the luggage of Marc Fogel, a history teacher who had worked in Russia since 2012; an American doctor had prescribed it for chronic pain. In June 2022 he was convicted of drug trafficking and sentenced to 14 years.

reports.title: Palau seizes 635 cannabis plants in Peleliu
reports.summary: Police seized 635 cannabis plants, 136 joints, about 250 lb of marijuana and $18,000 in cash in Peleliu; four Bangladeshi suspects were arrested. Police estimated the retail value at more than $400,000.

reports.title: Transnistria sends a personal grower’s harvest case to court
reports.summary: Investigators sent Ivan Zavyazkin’s case to court after police found 34 cannabis plants and 749.054 g of dried cannabis at his cottage in an October 2020 search.

reports.title: Police find a four-plant cannabis grow in a Tap Seac flat
reports.summary: Judiciary Police arrested a 28-year-old Taiwanese man and a 22-year-old local man after finding four cannabis plants, a portable greenhouse, a heating lamp, seeds and growing equipment in a rented flat near Tap Seac. The pair had met a year earlier, and police said they believed the plants were grown for sale. Officers came across the operation while investigating another drug case.

reports.title: Five years for a suitcase of hashish at Doha airport
reports.summary: A man whose suitcase was picked out by a scanner at Hamad International Airport was sentenced to five years in prison, a fine of 300,000 riyals and deportation. He said a friend at home, who had promised him a job in Qatar and paid for his ticket, had given him the case to deliver.

reports.title: Turkmenistan opens a drug incinerator and burns 122.5 kg
reports.summary: President Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow opened a drug-disposal complex 100 km north of Ashgabat on 2 December 2020. More than 122.5 kg of narcotics seized by the Interior Ministry were burned in its furnaces. The government presented the facility as a sign of its commitment to drug control; it did not say which drugs made up the total.

reports.title: Togo seizes 1.5 tonnes of cannabis hidden in a bus
reports.summary: Security officials in Lomé presented 1,541.60 kg of cannabis and three arrested suspects after stopping a bus arriving from Ghana during the night of 14–15 September. According to the authorities, the cannabis was hidden among second-hand clothing and was being taken to Benin through Togo.

reports.title: Marshall Islands reports suspended jail term for a personal cannabis import
reports.summary: A January newspaper report described a six-month suspended sentence and a $1,000 fine for Gandhi Heine after he pleaded guilty to importing marijuana. His lawyer said the cannabis was for personal use to relieve back pain.[@1] Chief Justice Carl Ingram approved the plea agreement, which included probation conditions restricting travel outside Majuro.[@1]

reports.title: Cocaine and cannabis packages found in the Line Islands
reports.summary: Police reported a 1.5 kg cocaine package and more than 3 kg of marijuana found in the Line Islands and taken to Betio headquarters. Police said illicit drugs were already in the country and warned that young people were probably using them; no arrest or outcome was reported.
