reports.title: Samoa destroys more than 10,000 cannabis plants
reports.summary: About 80 officers, using drones, raided six plantations in the Faleatiu hills and destroyed more than 10,000 cannabis plants; 11 people were arrested. Police valued the crop at about ST$10 million at ST$1,000 a plant. The area had been raided in 2015 and 2016, and officers reported guns being pointed at them.

reports.title: Police clear 5,500 cannabis plants from Guadalcanal's Mbarande area
reports.summary: On 21 and 22 October 2019 a joint RSIPF team uprooted more than 5,500 marijuana plants at several locations in Mbarande, North East Guadalcanal. No one was arrested at the time, and police asked village chiefs, church leaders and youth leaders to help identify the growers.

reports.title: Palau burns more than a tonne of cannabis in Peleliu
reports.summary: Police seized and burned over a tonne of marijuana from about 20 houses in Peleliu. It was one of the largest cannabis seizures in Palau and showed the scale of local cultivation.

reports.title: Home-grown cannabis is trafficked to Gabon via the Muni river
reports.summary: Cannabis is cultivated in Equatorial Guinea, with some of the product trafficked to Gabon via the Muni river, according to the 2019 United States OSAC crime and safety report for the country.[@1]

reports.title: Northern Cyprus reports counselling 98 people on supervised release
reports.summary: The Social Services Department reported regular interviews and psychosocial support for 98 people benefiting from the supervised-release law. The figure covered drug users together; the report gave no separate cannabis count.[@1] It documented the support work following the 2016 law’s treatment alternative to sentencing.[@1,2]

reports.title: Solomon Islands police intercept a cannabis parcel bound for Kiribati
reports.summary: Aviation security detected a suspicious box on a Solomon Airlines flight to Kiribati and police found cannabis. Two people, including an airline employee, were charged with attempted export and appeared in the Honiara Magistrates' Court in late July 2019. The amount was not stated.

reports.title: A journalist's arrest puts Russia's drug article on trial
reports.summary: Moscow police arrested the investigative reporter Ivan Golunov on drug charges; they published photographs of a drug laboratory and then admitted that only one had been taken in his flat. Three leading newspapers ran the same front page, the case was dropped after four days, and five officers were later sentenced to between 5 and 12 years. The case revived calls to soften Article 228.

reports.title: Torit police report two arrests over four sacks of cannabis
reports.summary: Torit police said they arrested a man and a woman over four sacks of bangi, each reported as 100 kg, transported from Ketire into the town. The spokesperson said the suspects were in custody during the investigation and would be sent to court.[@1]

reports.title: Myanmar police raid an American's hemp plantation
reports.summary: Police raided a 20-acre plantation on an industrial estate in Ngunzun township, Mandalay region, and arrested the American entrepreneur John Frederic Todoroki and two Myanmar employees. Six days later the region's chief minister said his government had allowed the firm to grow fibre plants for one year. Todoroki was released on medical bail in July 2019 and reportedly left the country.

reports.title: Vanuatu suspends a young cannabis seller’s ten-month prison sentence
reports.summary: Kaston Niawiye received concurrent ten-month sentences, suspended for two years, for possession, cultivation and sale of cannabis, plus twelve months’ supervision.[@1] He had been eighteen when he sold rolls for an older relative; the court found no evidence that he grew his ten plants commercially or personally shared the sale proceeds.[@1] The judgment applied the personal-growing guidance…

reports.title: An Iraqi court fines personal-use offenders; inspectors challenge the amounts
reports.summary: A Badra court imposed one-million-dinar fines in three personal-use drug cases, relying on general sentencing mitigation to impose a fine alone.[@1] Judicial inspectors said that choosing a fine did not allow judges to go below the drug law's five-million-dinar minimum, and recommended appeals against the judgments.[@1] Their later published review concerns drug offences generally and does not…

reports.title: Serbia’s top court keeps three years for preparing cannabis to sell
reports.summary: Marko Luković’s three-year prison sentence stood after the top court found that drying cannabis flowers and packaging them for sale amounted to drug production. He had collected flowers near the Morava and later carried the prepared cannabis to Kraljevo for sale. The court distinguished this processing from growing a plant, which then had a separate six-month-to-five-year penalty.

reports.title: Northern Cyprus jails a man for three plants and a small cannabis import
reports.summary: Arda Çelik received eighteen months in prison after growing three cannabis plants from seeds brought from Amsterdam and importing 3 g from the south of the island. The Nicosia court noted that cultivation carried a fifteen-year statutory maximum and treated the combined offences as serious.

reports.title: Bahrain jails a home cannabis grower and acquits him of selling
reports.summary: A 56-year-old former flight attendant received three years in prison and a 1,000-dinar fine after convictions involving growing cannabis at home and unlawful possession of a weapon and ammunition, The Daily Tribune reported.[@1] Police had raided his home after a tip-off; he said he grew for himself and learned online.[@1] The court acquitted him of selling because the evidence was…

reports.title: Guinea defence challenges cannabis charges against eleven young men
reports.summary: Eleven young men appeared in Dixinn after cannabis arrests in Ratoma; prosecutors sought prison for some and acquittal for four. Their lawyer challenged the possession evidence and the requested fines, arguing that the law linked fines to the value of drugs seized.

reports.title: Bahrain hands down its first death sentences for hashish trafficking
reports.summary: On 31 December 2018 the First High Criminal Court sentenced two of seven defendants to death for possessing, cultivating, smuggling and dealing in drugs; more than 18.5 kg of hashish was involved, and each was fined BHD10,000. It was the first time Bahraini courts imposed death for a non-lethal drug offence.

reports.title: Sudan’s Supreme Court upholds a life sentence for hashish trafficking
reports.summary: In Sudan Government v. Z. A. A. J., the National Supreme Court confirms an article 15 conviction involving 657.3 grams of hashish found in the accused’s locked bag. It treats the quantity as evidence of trafficking intent, upholds life imprisonment and reduces the fine to 10,000 pounds.

reports.title: Tonga seizes 2,665 cannabis plants in Vava'u
reports.summary: Police seized 2,665 cannabis plants at Mataika in Vava'u on 24 September 2018 and charged seven people. Media called it Tonga's largest cannabis bust at the time, though a 2017 raid at Matahau had found 3,894 plants.

reports.title: Jordan's cannabis seizures triple in five years
reports.summary: Cannabis seizures tripled from 444 kg to 1,478 kg between 2013 and 2018, a 233 percent increase that authorities read as a sign of increased national drug use.[@1]

reports.title: Transnistrian police seize a woman’s cannabis grown for rubbing tinctures
reports.summary: During the Mak-2018 campaign, police in the Dubossary district found thirteen cannabis plants and one poppy in a 55-year-old woman’s garden.

reports.title: Kiribati fines a fisheries officer who kept and used cannabis
reports.summary: Fisheries officer Tebaatei Kourabi received a fine after being convicted of keeping cannabis he had found and used for about a month.

reports.title: Police seize 400 kg of cannabis trafficked from DR Congo
reports.summary: Police intercepted a car on the Rubavu–Nyabihu road carrying 320 kg of cannabis and a motorcycle in Rubavu carrying 80 kg, after residents tipped them off. The drivers escaped, but police said they had identified the traffickers.

reports.title: São Tomé port police seize over a kilogram of cannabis on a Lagos ship
reports.summary: Police detained a Nigerian crew member and a São Toméan alleged accomplice after intercepting more than a kilogram of liamba, or cannabis, at São Tomé’s port.[@1] Criminal investigation police director Suleimany Tenjua said the seizure involved a ship on the Lagos–São Tomé route; the two detainees were to be brought before the judicial authorities.[@1] State news agency STP-PRESS reported the…

reports.title: Sudanese police destroy 500 cannabis farms in a month
reports.summary: A force of 366 men with 29 vehicles, a helicopter and drones spent the harvest month in El Radoom, destroyed about 500 farms and seized more than 30,000 packages of cannabis and 54,000 pieces of hashish. An armed group ambushed them and two officers were wounded.

reports.title: Timor-Leste gives an Australian 3½ years in a suspected cannabis-plant case
reports.summary: A Dili court sentenced Australian resident Tony Crean to three and a half years in prison in a case involving cannabis plants, according to Lusa.[@1] The report says he was convicted for possession and trafficking but acquitted of consumption after a negative urine test.[@1] He had been held since January, and his defence said it would appeal.[@1]

reports.title: Vanuatu gives eight villagers community work for cannabis offences
reports.summary: Eight first offenders from Bankir village on Malekula each received fifty hours of community work and six months’ probation for cannabis cultivation or possession.[@1] The case concerned conduct dating to 2009, with several defendants describing single small plants.[@1] The judge applied the 2013 personal-growing guidance and warned one defendant that his church belief did not permit him to…

reports.title: Vanuatu gives community work to a man who grew cannabis to deter rats
reports.summary: Roro Iauko received sixty hours of community service after admitting that he had planted twenty-six cannabis plants as a pest barrier in his garden.[@1] The judge accepted that the crop was intended for horticultural use, but ruled that this purpose did not provide a defence to unlawful cultivation.[@1] Applying the 2013 guidance, he placed the case at the lower end of the personal-growing…

reports.title: Tonga seizes 3,894 cannabis plants at Matahau
reports.summary: Police seized 3,894 cannabis plants from six bush allotments at Matahau and Fou'i on 4 May 2017 and arrested eight men. Four were sentenced on 7 June 2018. It appears to have been larger than the Vava'u bust that media later called Tonga's biggest.

reports.title: Hamas court sentences two drug dealers to death
reports.summary: A Hamas military court in Gaza sentenced two men to death for drug dealing, the first such verdicts since Hamas took power in 2007. One was to be executed by firing squad and the other was sentenced in absentia; the interior ministry said police had seized $2 million of drugs in January, mostly cannabis and narcotics.

reports.title: Timor-Leste holds an Australian before trial over five cannabis plants
reports.summary: An Australian resident entered pretrial custody in Dili in a case involving five suspected cannabis plants, according to Lusa reporting.[@1] Prosecutors had challenged an earlier decision allowing him to remain outside prison with reporting requirements and a confiscated passport, and the appeal court backed detention.[@1] The case later led to a three-and-a-half-year prison sentence, with the…

reports.title: Jamaica's courts see far fewer cannabis cases after decriminalisation
reports.summary: According to Harm Reduction International, court cases for possessing or smoking cannabis fell by more than 90 per cent after the reform of April 2015, and criminal cases referred to the courts in 2016 were 25 per cent fewer than in 2014. In 2016 the government nearly doubled its budget for the national HIV response, from 2.83 to 5.17 million US dollars.

reports.title: Kiribati fines a sailor whose prescribed marijuana was a prohibited import
reports.summary: Portuguese sailor Joao Afonso was fined A$1,600 on a marijuana charge after the court accepted that it was part of his prescribed treatment but held it was a prohibited import in Kiribati.

reports.title: Belize City openly sells tourist cannabis, charge dismissed
reports.summary: An American cruise-ship tourist arrested for buying 1.8 g of cannabis in Belize City had her charges dismissed: the judge noted the cannabis had been sold to her openly and she appeared to believe it was legal, cautioning her never to possess drugs in Belize again.[@1]

reports.title: Palestinian police uproot 2,000 cannabis saplings in Yasid
reports.summary: Police raided seven greenhouses in the village of Yasid, north of Nablus, and seized more than 2,000 cannabis saplings. Two suspects were arrested after they tried to flee; the raid was part of a West Bank crackdown that also seized 370 plants and 54 kg of dried cannabis in Jenin.

reports.title: Kiribati jails a sailor and confiscates his yacht in a cannabis case
reports.summary: Lyderic Morlier received nine months in prison and total fines of A$4,400 after admitting drug cultivation, prohibited import and immigration offences. The prison terms ran together, with credit for time already spent in custody.[@1,2] The court also confiscated his yacht, two engines, vessel-monitoring equipment and radios under the drug law.[@1]

reports.title: Panama burns thousands of marijuana plants on a Darien island
reports.summary: In September 2015 Panamanian soldiers uprooted and burned thousands of marijuana plants on a remote island in the Darien.[@1]

reports.title: Islamic State films itself burning a Syrian cannabis farm
reports.summary: After taking the town of Akhtarin, north of Aleppo, from the Free Syrian Army, fighters of the Islamic State cut down a field of cannabis, soaked it in fuel and set it alight for the camera.

reports.title: Syria's courts report a jump in drug cases
reports.summary: A judicial source told a government newspaper that 620 drug cases had come before the courts in four months, 115 of them in Damascus, against fewer than 500 in the whole of 2013. He recalled that trafficking carries ten years to death under the 1993 law, that whoever plants cannabis is treated as a trader, and that the law regards addicts as the victims of dealers.

reports.title: An Alabama veteran gets life without parole for a marijuana garden
reports.summary: Police looking for stolen property in 2011 found a few dozen marijuana plants at the house Lee Carroll Brooker, a disabled veteran with chronic pain, shared with his son in Alabama. Weighed with stalks and leaves, the plants came to about 2.8 pounds, over the 2.2-pound trafficking threshold.

reports.title: Isle of Man offers drug education to eligible first-time possession offenders
reports.summary: A Drug Arrest Referral Scheme introduced in 2014 let eligible first offenders caught with small personal quantities complete drug education and receive a caution. The government's 2024 review says most referrals involved cannabis, especially among under-18s, and records 93 completions from 108 entrants in 2021/22.

reports.title: Kuwait resumes hangings after a six-year pause
reports.summary: Kuwait hanged three men in April 2013 and two more in June, the first executions since 2007. All five were convicted of murder or rape; no drug offender was among them. The hangings ended a de facto moratorium that had lasted since 2007, in a country whose drug law already allowed death for trafficking.

reports.title: Cannabis farms spread in Kobane after the regime withdraws
reports.summary: After Kurdish forces took Kobane from Assad's army in July 2012, marijuana growing spread through the surrounding villages and onto rooftops in the town. The local Asayish spokesman told Rudaw that almost every village was growing it and that nobody had been arrested because nearly everyone was involved and the villagers were armed.

reports.title: Nearly 38,000 people are imprisoned in Indonesia for using cannabis in four years
reports.summary: Between 2009 and 2012, 37,923 people were imprisoned for using cannabis, according to figures cited by the Transnational Institute, even though the 2009 narcotics law and a Supreme Court circular were meant to send users to rehabilitation.

reports.title: Sughd destroys 400,000 wild hemp plants and seizes 113 kg of hashish
reports.summary: Police in Sughd destroyed about 400,000 wild hemp plants in Khujand, Asht and Bobojon Gafurov districts during operation «Мак-2012». Over the same period, officers in the region seized more than 113 kg of hashish and opened 98 criminal cases under Articles 200 and 201. The operation began on 20 May and was due to run until 30 November.

reports.title: Libya abolishes its anti-narcotics agency
reports.summary: After the 2011 uprising, the transitional cabinet dissolved the Anti-Narcotics and Psychotropic Substances Agency and moved its assets, staff and powers to the Interior Ministry. The agency had been created in 2006. Drug enforcement passed to the ministry.

reports.title: A Welshman gets eleven years in Malta for growing cannabis
reports.summary: Daniel Holmes, a 35-year-old Briton arrested in 2006 in Gozo, was convicted of importing seeds, cultivating cannabis in circumstances suggesting it was not for personal use and trafficking over 1 kg, a weight his defence said counted the whole dry plant. He was sentenced to eleven years and a fine of over €23,000. He said he grew it for himself.

reports.title: Transnistria counts 241 prisoners serving drug sentences
reports.summary: The justice ministry reported 241 people imprisoned for drug offences, 11% of its sentenced prison population, and more than 200 people serving suspended sentences under supervision.

reports.title: Liberia’s drug cases mostly end with on-the-spot fines, assessors report
reports.summary: A regional evaluation reported that most investigated drug-possession and trafficking cases ended with on-the-spot fines, and that only one drug conviction had been recorded in 2010. Officers lacked a forensic laboratory and relied on old UN-donated testing kits. The report called for a stronger anti-trafficking law; Liberia adopted a new drug statute in 2014.

reports.title: Libya's revolution breaks the state's drug controls
reports.summary: The uprising that began in February 2011 ended the central state's monopoly on force, and the security vacuum that followed weakened control of Libya's borders and ports. Trafficking networks expanded through the country over the next decade. The cannabis ban stayed on the books, but enforcement became local and uneven.

reports.title: A Briton gets four years in Dubai for a speck of cannabis on his shoe
reports.summary: Keith Brown, a youth worker from the English Midlands, was stopped in transit at Dubai airport in September 2009. Customs found 0.003 grams of cannabis, invisible to the eye, in the tread of his shoe. He was sentenced to four years, then the minimum for possession. Another traveller was reported jailed over three poppy seeds from a bread roll.

reports.title: Grenada seizes 460 kg of cannabis in 2009
reports.summary: Grenadian authorities seized 460 kg of cannabis and 1,309 cannabis cigarettes during 2009, as reported in the US International Narcotics Control Strategy Report.[@1,2]

reports.title: Zambia's drug agency enlists chiefs against cannabis
reports.summary: The Drug Enforcement Commission met traditional leaders to persuade farmers to grow food and cash crops instead of cannabis; chiefs reported growers to the agency. The campaign was an enforcement and crop-substitution effort, not a change in the law.

reports.title: Al-Shabaab flogs men for hashish in Kismayo
reports.summary: After Al-Shabaab seized the port city of Kismayo, three local men were arrested for possession of hashish. Their supply was burned and they were publicly flogged by the militants.

reports.title: Marshall Islands court counts two marijuana-selling cases in Majuro
reports.summary: The High Court's 2008 annual report recorded 27 criminal cases filed in Majuro, two of them for selling marijuana. The same caseload included 13 assault cases, four burglaries or larcenies and three sexual assaults, so cannabis sales were a small part of the serious criminal work. The report gives case counts, not arrest or seizure figures.

reports.title: A Tejen cannabis grower and seed seller are sentenced to 10 and 11 years
reports.summary: A man bought cannabis seed at a bazaar in Tejen in March 2008, planted it in his garden and produced 153 grams of marijuana, which he sold for $100. A court sentenced the two men involved to 11 and 10 years in prison. The US State Department's 2010 narcotics report cited the case as an example of how small-scale cannabis growing was punished.

reports.title: A Moroccan resin route through Mali is identified
reports.summary: In early 2007 a route for smuggling cannabis resin from Morocco through Mauritania, Mali, Niger and Chad and on into either Egypt or Sudan was identified.[@1] A total of 5.7 tons of cannabis resin was seized in five seizures in Niger in the 2006–2007 period.[@1] The case put Mali on a trans-Saharan trafficking map linking Moroccan resin to markets further east.[@1]

reports.title: Niger seizes 5.7 tons of Moroccan resin in transit
reports.summary: Five seizures in Niger in the 2006–2007 period netted a total of 5.7 tons of cannabis resin moving along the newly identified trans-Saharan route from Morocco through Mauritania, Mali and Niger toward Chad and on into Egypt or Sudan.[@1] The seizures made Niger the most visible interception point on that route.[@1]

reports.title: Drugs-for-arms barter reported as PNG tops Oceanian cannabis use
reports.summary: Reports described barter trade exchanging illicit drugs for arms in the coastal cities of Lae, Madang, Wewak and Port Moresby.[@1] Papua New Guinea shared with Micronesia the highest prevalence of cannabis abuse in Oceania, and cannabis plants were also illicitly cultivated in Fiji, Samoa and Tonga.[@1]

reports.title: UNODC records three tonnes of herb seized in Burkina Faso over 2000–2005
reports.summary: The annex to UNODC's 2007 Cannabis in Africa overview records 3,004 kilograms of cannabis herb seized in Burkina Faso over the years 2000 to 2005.[@1]

reports.title: Macau’s top court treats shared-cost cannabis supply as trafficking
reports.summary: Macau’s top court upheld a cannabis trafficking conviction, ruling that providing cannabis to other people counted as supply even when they shared the purchase cost.[@1] The old law’s lesser-quantity tier used a three-day personal-use reference, which the court placed at six to eight grams for cannabis; the quantity supplied exceeded it.[@1] Macau’s 2009 replacement later introduced a…

reports.title: Nauru's Supreme Court upholds three-month sentences for Indian hemp
reports.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed appeals against three-month sentences for possessing Indian hemp under section 10(1)(c) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1968. It was the last reported pre-2004 cannabis prosecution and showed the old law's three-month statutory minimum.

reports.title: Northern Mariana Islands’ crop raids shift cannabis supply toward imports
reports.summary: A federal drug assessment linked the decline of local cannabis growing in 2000–2001 to eradication campaigns and a greater reliance on supplies from the Philippines and Palau. It reported a sharp rise in retail prices and said local cultivation was largely confined to small amounts for personal use.

reports.title: A US cable details the cannabis trade and Maoist taxes
reports.summary: A confidential US embassy cable from June 2003 reported that Nepal was a source country for cannabis sold in India and for hashish sent to North America, Europe and South-East Asia. The Narcotic Drug Control Law Enforcement Unit told the embassy that Maoist insurgents levied a tax of up to 35 percent on cannabis cultivation and transport, and that trucks could hide 500-700 kg.

reports.title: Guernsey leaves a pub licensee's cannabis conviction standing despite doubts
reports.summary: The Court of Appeal left Heather Guest's conviction for permitting cannabis-resin smoking at the Helmsman pub undisturbed, despite doubts about whether the conviction was safe. Convicted in 2002 and sentenced to six weeks in prison, she said she ejected suspected smokers. The judges considered their powers too limited to set aside the conviction on the basis of those doubts.[@1]

reports.title: Syria and Lebanon clear the Bekaa cannabis fields
reports.summary: After cannabis and opium production returned to the Syrian-controlled Bekaa in 2001, Syrian and Lebanese authorities ran a joint eradication campaign from 2002 to 2004 that sharply cut the area under cannabis and opium. Syria also upgraded its counternarcotics branch to a directorate in 2002 and opened regional offices in Aleppo and Homs to watch the Turkish and Lebanese borders.

reports.title: Maoists tax cannabis as police leave Makwanpur
reports.summary: In the Maoist-held villages of north-western Makwanpur, police had stopped patrolling and farmers turned to cannabis as their main cash crop. A Nepali Times report said the Maoists had first declared the area a marijuana-free zone, then allowed the trade in exchange for a cut. Police had seized 8,000 kg of cannabis and destroyed the crop on 74.5 hectares the year before.

reports.title: Hong Kong keeps a two-month sentence for selling two cannabis cigarettes
reports.summary: Chor Lui’s two-month prison sentence stood after he sold an undercover officer two cannabis cigarettes containing 0.24 g for HK$30.[@1] The appeal judge considered his prior drug convictions and the commercial sale in a discotheque important despite the small amount, while recognising the then-lower sentencing benchmark for herbal cannabis than resin.[@1]

reports.title: A Nepali Times investigation finds a Rs 6 billion ganja trade
reports.summary: A December 2000 investigation in Makwanpur, Bara, Parsa and Dhading found cannabis plantations worked openly, with Indian buyers supplying seed on credit and returning at harvest. The paper estimated Nepal grew 3 million kg of ganja and charas a year and exported Rs 6 billion worth to India, with police, local officials and Maoist cadres taking a share.

reports.title: Seychelles court uses wrapped resin portions as evidence of trafficking
reports.summary: The Supreme Court convicted Robin Francois of trafficking after finding that he knowingly possessed 166.4 g of cannabis resin. It treated the individually wrapped portions as evidence of preparation for supply, while explaining that the presumption above 25 g could be rebutted.

reports.title: Dakar port seizure exposes a Moroccan-resin route via Sierra Leone
reports.summary: In July 2000 the Senegalese authorities seized some 5.3 tons of cannabis resin of Moroccan origin at the port of Dakar.[@1] The resin had been shipped by sea in freight containers and was allegedly destined to be smuggled via Sierra Leone into the Netherlands.[@1] The case showed Senegal working both as a cannabis producer and as a transit point for Moroccan resin bound for Europe.[@1]

reports.title: Hong Kong cuts a repeat offender’s cannabis-possession sentence to two months
reports.summary: Phung Hai’s six-month prison sentence for possessing 1.18 g of cannabis was reduced to two months on appeal.[@1] The original magistrate had relied on two earlier drug convictions to reject a fine, but the appeal judge accepted that the sentence was excessive in light of the sentencing authorities; the prosecution did not defend it.[@1]
